paper.title_en: A High Precision Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
paper.abstract_en: We present a Transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. Given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts 512 quintic B-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1620,160]M$ ($M$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $C^4$ time-domain waveforms with exact parameter and temporal derivatives via automatic differentiation. The model is pretrained jointly on numerical-relativity (NR) waveforms from the SXS and RIT catalogues together with synthetic NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv5PHM, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on SXS strain data. On 109 SXS evaluation waveforms (106 physical systems) over $[-1500,100]M$, it achieves a mean balanced relative strain error of 0.0305 and a mean finite-window detector mismatch at $120\,M_\odot$ of 0.1536%, outperforming SEOBNRv5PHM, NRSur7dq4v2, and IMRPhenomTPHM across common support, with compiled batched float64 inference reaching 445 waveforms/s on an A100 GPU.
